headline: Large User Grid Cost Shift
short_summary: This bill aims to shift electricity costs for grid infrastructure from residential customers to large energy users, primarily data centers, potentially lowering residential bills.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Senator Louise Lucas, Delegate Destiny LeVere Bolling, Dominion Energy, residential customers, ratepayer advocates.
opponents: Data Center Coalition (initially concerned about language), potentially large industrial users.
news_headline: Virginia bill aims to cut residential energy costs by shifting expenses to data centers.
news_summary: A bill, HB 1393 (and its companion SB 253), aims to shift energy costs, including capacity auction prices and new distribution infrastructure, onto high-load users like data centers and large manufacturers. This shift is projected to save residential customers around $5.52 per month, while increasing costs for data centers by approximately 15-16%.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates water users supplying data centers to report their total monthly or quarterly water consumption, including reclaimed water, to the State Water Control Board, enhancing transparency.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Senator Kannan Srinivasan, Potomac Conservancy, environmental and conservation groups, local planning and public health organizations.
opponents: Data center operators (historically shielded water usage as "trade secrets").
news_headline: Virginia, home to hundreds of data centers, adds new restrictions.
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed bills, including SB 553, to regulate data centers by requiring water utilities to report aggregate data center water consumption. This measure aims to provide transparency on water use, which has been a growing concern due to the significant water demands of data centers.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise
short_summary: This bill requires site assessments for new high energy use facilities, including data centers, to evaluate their sound profile on nearby residential areas and schools, and allows localities to assess other environmental impacts.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Delegate Josh Thomas, Senator Danica Roem (for similar SB 94), environmental and conservation groups, neighborhood and parent associations, local planning and public health organizations.
opponents: Data center developers, tech industry trade groups, chambers of commerce, commercial real estate associations, pro-growth business or utility groups (concerned about permitting delays and added costs).
news_headline: Virginia, home to hundreds of data centers, adds new restrictions.
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed bills, including HB 153, to regulate data centers by introducing new siting requirements for large facilities. This legislation mandates impact assessments, including noise studies for nearby homes and schools, and allows for reviews of potential impacts on water, agriculture, and historic sites.
